newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INSURERS SEE INVESTMENT OPENINGS IN EMU.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INSURERS SEE INVESTMENT OPENINGS IN EMU.

text.p: Insurance companies will have more opportunities to diversify investment portfolios and find better risk/return ratios once Europe's single currency is in place, the head of a Finnish insurance lobby said.

"Diversifying investment portfolios will become easier and it will be possible for companies to find better risk/return ratios on investment," Arto Ojala, managing director of the Federation of Finnish Insurance Companies, said in an interview in the 6/1996 issue of industry trade letter Vakuutussanomat.
Finnish insurers' investments in assets that are now in foreign currencies would grow once the euro is in use, he said.

"When investments abroad increase, the importance of being familiar with markets and clearing systems will be emphasised," Ojala said, pointing to the need of training staff in the run-up to the third phase of EMU, scheduled to begin in January 1999.
"The insurance business -- like all other sectors -- must wake up. There are less than 600 working days left to EMU," he noted.
